findings.text: the newly added refusal for an unavailable scontrol is not held by any test: deleting the except OSError handler around the scontrol call leaves the suite at 38 passed, EXIT=0, replayed on a mutated copy of the 129a365f tree. The consequence is caller-facing rather than cosmetic: the executes of an absent scontrol escapes as OSError instead of the ValueError the docstring and the anchor promise, so a caller written to catch ValueError for a refusal that cannot be resolved would abort instead of falling back to the unknown-host marker; latent only because receipts_host has no production caller today.

a single token that scontrol cannot parse but echoes verbatim is returned as a host: scontrol show hostnames None prints None to stdout, one line, exit 0, so the expansion's one-line test passes and None is returned as a node name. No live input reached it here — 15,638 sacct rows from 2026-09-01 onward contain no empty or None NodeList, and a job that does not exist reports nothing at all — so the path is unreachable on this cluster's measured history rather than refused by the code, and the anchor's never inferred clause is only as strong as that history staying true.

the purged-job fixture models sacct exiting 1 with empty stdout, while the live measurement for a job that does not exist on this cluster is exit 0 with empty stdout; the refusal is the same on both because the empty stdout alone fails the one-line test, so the test's conclusion holds and only its rc shape is one this cluster did not produce.

item_verdicts.diff: read as one commit over five files; receipts_host now makes two reads at telemetry_index.py:368-403, requiring exactly one sacct line and exactly one expanded line, and the two replacement tests feed the compressed and truncated tokens this cluster actually prints.
item_verdicts.done_when: the measure is met at this head: 38 passed at 129a365f against a 34-passed base, the whole-tree lint gate green at 129a365f, a declared mutation quoted verbatim beside the tests it reddens, and each measurement log naming the revision whose content it measured.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal's third clause — a helper that refuses rather than guesses — now holds for every multi-node shape measured on this cluster, where at the first round it held for four of five, and the two clauses the first round confirmed still hold unchanged at this head.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it reports complete at 129a365f, names the four findings and how each was repaired, and its stated numbers reproduced here — 38 against 34, ruff exit 0, the control's mutation and the two tests it reddens, and the module-path print that shows the gate measured the worktree rather than the main checkout.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the repair commit touches exactly the five fenced paths — imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py, tests/test_telemetry_index.py, docs/evidence/archive/serve-telemetry-spine-landed.html, docs/figures/serve-telemetry-spine/hostless-row-resolution.svg, docs/plans/serve-telemetry-spine.html — and no other file, with the plan's version and modified meta lines untouched.

justifications.durability: the two guards that carry the repair are held — the argv assertion reddens when -P is removed and the expansion test reddens when the line count stops being required, both measured — and the refusal is now exercised against real cluster output; docked four because the newly added scontrol-unavailability refusal is unheld, the suite staying at 38 passed when its handler is deleted (FINDING 1), so the caller-facing contract for an absent scontrol rests on nothing.
justifications.evidence: every number in the repair's manifest reproduced here from the head content — 38 passed at 129a365f, the control's reddening of two named tests, the module path proving which tree ran — and the replacement fixtures were checked against live sacct and scontrol output rather than the author's description; docked two because one fixture's rc shape is not what this cluster emitted (FINDING 3) and no log yet exists for a live refusal of the helper outside a mock.
justifications.fit: the repair names its mechanism — two reads, one expanded line — in the docstring, the commit body and the anchor alike, so code, record and evidence now say the same thing; docked one because the docstring's claim that a still-running job resolves to nothing usable is broader than the code, which resolves a running single-node job to its node.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the refusal the plan required is now held for every multi-node shape measured live on this cluster and the single-node path still resolves, so the third clause is delivered; docked one because the never-inferred wording rests on an echo path that no measurement reaches today (FINDING 2).
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff lists the five fenced paths and nothing else, the plan change is confined to the run's own section body, and no meta line or neighbouring section moved.

Read: the repair commit's five-file diff, the run's updated manifest and its five logs, the repaired receipts_host and the two replacement tests. Independently re-derived here: the gate at a git-archive of 129a365f (38 passed, EXIT=0, log recheck-gate-head.log), a refusal probe of receipts_host over seven real job ids taken live from this cluster's sacct (log recheck-probe-real-inputs.log), live sacct and scontrol stream measurements behind each fixture, the base build's byte identity to d9e89c5b, and one declared mutation round (log recheck-negative-control.log).

Q1 MULTI-NODE REFUSAL. The refusal fires for every multi-node shape this cluster produces. Probed live through the repaired code, module path printed as /run/user/39486/recheck-head/imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py: job 1269885 (98dci4-clu-[3014-3015], two contiguous nodes) REFUSED; 1268941 (98dci4-clu-[3001,3054], two non-contiguous) REFUSED; 1271014 (98dci4-clu-[3034-3035]) REFUSED; 1207375 (98dci4-clu-[5073-5086], fourteen) REFUSED naming all fourteen; 1222419 (98dci4-clu-[4009-4018,4041-4045], two ranges) REFUSED; 1232722 (ten scattered nodes) REFUSED; 1999999 (job does not exist) REFUSED. Positive control, so the instrument is shown able to succeed: 1273253 and 1271709 both RETURNED 98dci4-gpu-0003, the node sacct and scontrol agree on. On the residual — whether any input still returns a hostlist token as a host — no hostlist token survives: the compressed token expands to more than one line and is refused, and the default-width truncation is doubly closed, since -P is now requested (measured: sacct -j 1207375 -X -n -o NodeList prints 98dci4-clu-[50+, -P prints the full 98dci4-clu-[5073-5086]) and a truncated token that reached the expansion anyway is refused because scontrol prints nothing to stdout for it (measured: stdout 0 bytes, stderr 34 bytes carrying Invalid hostlist: 98dci4-clu-[50+, rc=0), leaving zero lines. One non-host path remains and is reported as FINDING 2 below.

Q2 TESTS MODEL REAL SHAPES. The replacement fixtures were compared against live sacct and scontrol output, not against the author's description. The fourteen-node expansion fixture (tests/test_telemetry_index.py:819) generates exactly the fourteen lines this cluster prints for 1207375, 98dci4-clu-5073 through 98dci4-clu-5086, verified line by line against scontrol show hostnames 98dci4-clu-[5073-5086]. The truncated fixture 98dci4-clu-[50+ at :829 is the live default-width output of the same job, byte for byte, and the test's claim that scontrol rejects it on stderr while exiting 0 and printing no node at all is what I measured on the live binary (stdout empty, stderr Invalid hostlist:, rc=0) rather than a claim resting on the fixture. The argv assertion at :785 holds -P against the live command form. The purged-job case at :823 is the one shape whose fixture differs from what this cluster emitted: it models sacct exiting 1 with empty stdout, and the live measurement for a job that does not exist is rc=0 with empty stdout — the refusal is the same on both, so the test's conclusion holds while its rc shape is not one this cluster produced here (FINDING 3).

Q3 ANCHOR. The anchor now describes the behaviour at this head. docs/evidence/archive/serve-telemetry-spine-landed.html:2420-2431 replaces the one-read claim with the two-read form — sacct -P for the node list, scontrol show hostnames to expand it, a node returned only when the expansion yields exactly one line — and states the refusal set as a name with no job id, an unavailable sacct or scontrol, or an expansion that is not exactly one node. That matches the code read at 129a365f: telemetry_index.py:362-403 raises on exactly those conditions. The cited evidence command was updated to the form that reproduces the record: sacct -j 1271709 -X -n -P -o NodeList prints 98dci4-gpu-0003, the node the surrounding paragraph claims. The one clause that overstates is a host is recorded or refused, never inferred, for the reason in FINDING 2.

Q4 LOG REVISIONS. Each log now carries the revision whose content it measured. host-attribution-gate.log stamps rev=129a365f and its stated command reproduces 38 passed there — I ran exactly that gate against a git-archive of 129a365f and got 38 passed, EXIT=0. host-attribution-ruff.log stamps rev=129a365f over the same tree. host-attribution-negative-control.log stamps rev=129a365f with the worktree path and its red log. host-attribution-baseline.log and host-attribution-repro.log stamp rev=d9e89c5b over tree=/tmp/host-attribution-base, and that build is the base content, not a label: its imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py is md5 85b21ef470603071934e8d29e854d91b, identical to git show d9e89c5b:imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py, carries the pre-repair line 413 self.host = host or os.uname().nodename and zero occurrences of scontrol. The round-one defect, where three logs stamped the base while measuring repaired content, is repaired: the base-labelled pair now measure a byte-verified base build and the three head-labelled logs measure 129a365f.

MUTATION ROUND. One further round was run, aimed at what nothing holds. The repair's own control (replacing the two-read lookup with nodes = completed.stdout.split(), requiring exactly one field) reddens two tests: test_the_receipts_host_is_resolved_from_the_job_id on the argv it loses, and test_a_job_that_does_not_resolve_is_refused_not_guessed with DID NOT RAISE — 2 failed, 36 passed, EXIT=1, so the two substantive guards, the -P flag and the one-expanded-line count, are held. My round removed the except OSError handler around the scontrol call, and the suite stayed green at 38 passed, EXIT=0: a round of mutation did demonstrate something further, and what it demonstrates is FINDING 1.
